 Kane Scores Winner in Record-Breaking England Appearance..."Next Goal is 100th International Goal"
 Yu Byeongmin 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.13 08:34 
 View 
 View Count 
 Enlarge image 
 ▲ Harry Kane celebrates scoring a goal. 
 Harry Kane marked his historic milestone as England's most-capped men's player by scoring the winning goal. 
 England secured a 2-1 victory over Croatia in their Group A3 home match of the 2026-2027 UEFA Nations League held at Wembley Stadium in London, England, on November 12 (local time). 
 This marked Kane's 126th international appearance. 
 Kane surpassed Peter Shilton (125 caps) to become the outright record-holder for the most appearances for the England national team. 
 With the score tied 1-1, Kane celebrated his record-breaking appearance in front of some 80,000 spectators by netting a penalty in the 19th minute of the second half. 
 It was also the 92nd international goal for Kane, who holds the record as England's all-time leading goalscorer. 
 He is now 39 goals ahead of second-place Wayne Rooney. 
 England took the lead in the 24th minute of the first half with an opener from Morgan Rogers, but conceded an equalizer to Petar Sučić in the 14th minute of the second half. 
 A defensive header error by England defender Jarell Quansah during a Croatian corner kick led to the goal. 
 Soon after, Quansah won a foul inside the penalty area. 
 Following a video assistant referee (VAR) review, the referee pointed to the penalty spot, and Kane stepped up to convert. 
 Maintaining second place in their group, England confirmed their advancement to the quarterfinals scheduled for March next year. 
 Group leader Spain also secured a quarterfinal spot by defeating the Czech Republic 2-0 on the same day. 
 England will face Spain away on November 15 to contest the top spot in the group. 
 A commemorative ceremony for Kane was held prior to the match. 
 Shilton, who held England's appearance record for 37 years after surpassing Bobby Moore (108 caps) in 1989, presented Kane with a commemorative gift, while Prince William handed him a jersey bearing the number 126. 
 Croatian captain Luka Modrić, a former Tottenham Hotspur teammate of Kane, presented a replica of a football first brought to Croatia by British entrepreneurs in 1880. 
 Enlarge image 
 Having won the Ballon d'Or last month, Kane's next target is his 100th international goal. 
 "I've talked with the boys about getting to 100," Kane said. "It's another huge milestone that I'll try to reach as quickly as possible." 
 Only three men have scored 100 or more international goals: Cristiano Ronaldo (Portugal), Lionel Messi (Argentina), and Ali Daei (Iran). 
 In League A Group 1 on the same day, Italy defeated France 3-1 at San Siro in Milan, propelled by a multi-goal performance from Francesco Pio Esposito. 
 This marks Italy's first home win over France since 1962. 
 Italy moved to the top of the group, holding the advantage in the head-to-head record against France. 
 France could have secured a quarterfinal berth with a draw in this match. 
 France got off to a good start. 
 In the 10th minute of the first half, Italian goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma made an error while clearing the ball, and French forward Michael Olise capitalized by intercepting it to find the back of the net. 
 However, Italy equalized in the 26th minute of the first half. 
 Nicolò Cambiaghi drove down the left flank and delivered a cutback for Esposito, who slotted it in near the front post. 
 The 21-year-old Esposito scored his 8th goal in his 14th international appearance. 
 Italy breathed a sigh of relief after two dangerous French shots hit the woodwork, while Francesco Esposito's older brother Sebastiano missed a penalty wide of the target. 
 While Davide Frattesi scored Italy's go-ahead goal in the 18th minute of the second half, younger brother Francesco sealed the victory in the 30th minute of the second half by converting a penalty earned by Antonio Vergara.
